title: Hong Kong outlines four-step AI ‘talent ladder’ to offset entry-level job shock
source_used: HKSAR Government press release (speech by Kevin Choi) via Bastille Post
key_facts: Kevin Choi, Hong Kong's Permanent Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry, spoke on 5 Oct 2026 at the Global Youth Powerhouse Summit.
He called the 'entry-level shock' real: routine first-job tasks like basic coding and customer service are tasks AI now does well.
Step 1: mass AI literacy, over 200 courses by early 2028, free training to upskill 40,000 employees.
Step 2: 27 new AI-related STEM degree programmes; about 500 Talent Foundry places a year.
Step 3: 30,000 Youth Employment and Internship Programme over two years, including about 10,000 STEM internships; a $10 billion research and industry scheme.
Step 4: infrastructure and policy: Sandy Ridge data cluster from mid-2027, a new Commissioner for AI in the Digital Policy Office.
quote_evidence: "The 'entry-level shock' in today's theme is real."
"Our answer is not to shield young people from AI, but to make sure the first job is still there, and that it is a better one."
why_it_matters_hint: A government plan to protect graduate jobs from AI.
